key_insight: Hyperlyve combines learning with formal verification to certify that nonlinear systems—including those controlled by neural networks—converge toward an equilibrium. Its key innovation is parallel enumeration of the regions induced by ReLU networks to support exact Lyapunov stability certification.
problem_solved: A neural controller may perform well in simulations without guaranteeing stability. Hyperlyve addresses the challenge of constructing and formally certifying neural Lyapunov functions for nonlinear dynamical systems.
method: Learn continuous piecewise-affine neural Lyapunov functions as candidates for proving asymptotic stability.
Use a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) loop to alternate between learning candidates and formally checking them.
Parallelize enumeration of the hyperplane arrangement induced by ReLU activations to support certification.
impact: Hyperlyve offers a path from empirical testing toward formal stability guarantees for neural-network-controlled systems. Parallel enumeration targets a computational bottleneck in verifying piecewise-affine neural models.
visual_elements: Feedback-loop diagram: dynamical system, neural controller, and stability verifier.

paper_title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
paper_authors: Brian Yarbrough, Jesse Wayment, Jingbo Wang, Philip E. Paré, Shreyas Sundaram
